In these experiments, participants were asked to perform tasks that required self-control, such as suppressing their emotions or resisting temptation. After engaging in these tasks, participants were found to have reduced self-control in subsequent tasks, indicating that their ability to regulate their behavior had been depleted.

Ego depletion has implications for understanding the limits of human willpower and the importance of managing and conserving self-control resources.
